recognition_note: The antigen was identified from the supplied pre-cutoff annotation as HSV-2 strain 333 glycoprotein D. I also recognized pre-cutoff solved complexes of this exact antigen surface with different binders: E317 (paper first public 2013-09-20; PDB 3W9E released 2013-10-02), Nb14 and Nb32 (paper first public 2025-05-06; PDB entries released 2025-05-28). None is the supplied antibody: in particular, the supplied and E317 H3s have only 16.7% identity over aligned IMGT H3 positions. Exact CDR searches in the launcher record and a cutoff-gated search attempted here did not identify the supplied antibody, so the supplied complex itself is not recognized.
what_separated_them: No candidate had Tier A evidence about this binder, so this remains a broad prior over surfaces. The narrow separation came from comparative calculations on every supplied footprint: connectivity, native-context accessibility risk, exact footprint extent versus the 39.29 A supplied paratope span, and coarse actual-paratope chemistry. I treated C2/C4/C8 as nested drawings of one receptor-groove family rather than counting their repeated E317 evidence three times; C5/C6 and C1/C7 likewise share surface priors. The receptor family received the largest cluster mass because three independent binders validate it, but the measured E317 transfer is weak (44.4% all-CDR identity, 16.7% H3), preventing concentration. C8 narrowly leads as the connected broad drawing; C3 is nearly tied because its cleft best matches the protruding H3 at a coarse level.
